original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Determine the exact positive destination-row tariff for dirty three-row demand (e,h,e+h) over F2[e,h]/(e,h)^2, and prove the resulting nineteen-vector frontier for nonprincipal zero-sum triples over commutative unital rings.
scope_change_reason: The donor explicitly assigned this algebraic problem after the merged two-row and local-ring boundary work. It is a scoped side result, not a replacement H2/K interface or an extension of an admitted bit supplier.
bottleneck_link: Provides a rigorously priced dirty-input identity and all-word lower bound in a complete abstract gate-price model. Applying it to a physical supplier still requires source access, coefficient, routing, precision, stock and full interface accounting; no selected-kappa improvement is claimed.
stop_rule: Finish when all price terms have matching words and an all-interleaving lower bound, or record a precise unresolved branch or counterexample within the 60-minute session. Restrict finite corroboration to four small rings and seven independent eight-element shortest-path cases.
evidence: README.md proves the nineteen-vector Pareto frontier and exact arbitrary-positive-price envelope. The self-contained verifier checks 102 demand triples in four rings, 1,938 matching words, 15,504 formal forward/inverse column checks, 155,648 literal input checks, strict exposure of all 19 vectors, eight controls and seven independent packed-state shortest paths. Finite checks corroborate the written proof; human review, proof-kernel acceptance and physical supplier admission are unclaimed.
author: lee-phys, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in source inspection, derivation, construction, Python implementation, finite experiments, verification and writing. No subagents or independent reviewers were used.

open_questions.question: What is the exact destination-row tariff for demand (3,5,6) in the Boolean product ring F2 x F2 x F2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The demand is zero-sum with incomparable component ideals but a principal total ideal. A verified one-insertion word beats the present formula, so a separate branch is necessary.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate and bound one-insertion restoring words, starting from the cost-16 word in README.md, then compare their envelope with multi-insertion words.
open_questions.blocked_by: The nonprincipal-ideal lower bound on the number of source calls does not apply; the cost-16 witness is only an upper bound.

open_questions.question: What is the exact tariff for (e,h,e+h) over the eight-element ring when every directed ADD edge has its own positive price?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Destination totals can conceal a cheaper sequence using a directed cycle and do not determine edge-sensitive optimality.
open_questions.first_step: Use a cheap directed three-cycle as a finite shortest-path probe and classify the source-support cases with edge counts retained.
open_questions.blocked_by: A per-edge two-call restoration lemma is false for three rows, as the retained five-ADD identity demonstrates.

open_questions.question: What is the exact tariff for the non-zero-sum demand (e,h,e+h+z) in F2[e,h,z]/(e,h,z)^2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The demand ideal needs three generators and the zero-sum constructions no longer reach the endpoint; cancelling unit insertions must still be considered.
open_questions.first_step: Find matching words for the cheapest insertion-support cases and test small positive-price regimes with full dirt tracking.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present theorem uses the zero-sum identity for all four indirect construction families and makes no claim about this demand.
